footer: You received this email because of activity on your Dimmi account. If it was not you, you can ignore it.

verify_email.subject: Verify your email address
verify_email.intro: Confirm that {{.email}} is your email address by opening this link.

magic_link.subject: Your Dimmi sign-in link
magic_link.intro: Open this link to sign in. It works once, within {{.minutes}} minutes.
magic_link.code: Or type this code on the sign-in page:
magic_link.requested: The request came from {{.ip}} ({{.device}}). If it was not you, ignore this email: nobody can sign in without it.

reset_password.subject: Reset your Dimmi password
reset_password.intro: Someone asked to reset the password of your account. Choose a new one here.
reset_password.expiry: The link works for 60 minutes. If you did not ask for it, ignore this email: your password stays as it is.

confirm_code.subject: Your Dimmi confirmation code
confirm_code.intro: Type this code to confirm it is you:
confirm_code.expiry: The code works for 10 minutes. If you did not ask for it, someone may be using your account: sign out of your other sessions.

password_changed.subject: Your Dimmi password changed
password_changed.changed: The password of your account was changed.
password_changed.reset: The password of your account was reset, and every other session was signed out.
password_changed.removed: Your email address was just proven, and the account had a password set before it was. That password may not be yours, so we removed it and signed out every other session. Set a new password in your security settings.

new_sign_in.subject: New sign-in to your Dimmi account
new_sign_in.intro: Your account was just signed in from {{.device}} at {{.ip}}.
new_sign_in.unknown: If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign that session out and change your password.

two_factor_enabled.subject: Two-factor authentication is on
two_factor_enabled.intro: Your account now asks for a code from your authenticator app at every sign-in, after your password or sign-in link.
two_factor_enabled.unknown: If this was not you, someone else may control your account: review your security settings and change your password.

two_factor_disabled.subject: Two-factor authentication is off
two_factor_disabled.intro: Your account no longer asks for a second factor when you sign in, and its recovery codes no longer work.
two_factor_disabled.unknown: If this was not you, change your password and turn two-factor authentication back on.

recovery_code_used.subject: A recovery code was used to sign in
recovery_code_used.intro: A recovery code was just used to sign in to your account. Codes left: {{.remaining}}.
recovery_code_used.regenerate: You are running out of recovery codes. Make a new set in your security settings now.
recovery_code_used.unknown: If this was not you, change your password and make new recovery codes.

two_factor_required.subject: {{.workspace}} now requires two-factor authentication
two_factor_required.intro: An admin of {{.workspace}} turned on two-factor authentication for everyone in the workspace.
two_factor_required.blocked: Until you add an authenticator app to your account, you cannot open the workspace. It takes a minute.

suspicious_sign_in_attempts.subject: Someone is trying to sign in to your Dimmi account
suspicious_sign_in_attempts.intro: Many wrong passwords were tried for your account in the last hour, so we locked it for unknown devices for a while.
suspicious_sign_in_attempts.advice: Devices you signed in from before still get in. If you use a short or reused password, change it now.

identity_linked.subject: {{.provider}} account linked to your Dimmi account
identity_linked.intro: A {{.provider}} account with your email address was linked to your Dimmi account. You can now sign in with {{.provider}}.
identity_linked.unknown: If this was not you, unlink it in your security settings and change your password.

workspace_deletion_scheduled.subject: {{.workspace}} was deleted
workspace_deletion_scheduled.intro: {{.deleted_by}} deleted the workspace {{.workspace}}. Its members lost access, its access tokens stopped working and its pending invitations were withdrawn.
workspace_deletion_scheduled.restore: Any owner can restore it until {{.date}}. After that, it and everything in it is deleted for good.

workspace_deletion_reminder.subject: {{.workspace}} will be deleted for good in a few days
workspace_deletion_reminder.intro: The workspace {{.workspace}} is in the trash and will be deleted for good on {{.date}}, with every conversation, contact and file in it.
workspace_deletion_reminder.restore: If that is a mistake, any owner can still restore it until then.

workspace_restored.subject: {{.workspace}} was restored
workspace_restored.intro: {{.restored_by}} restored the workspace {{.workspace}}. Its members can work in it again.
workspace_restored.revoked: Access tokens and invitations ended by the deletion stay ended: create new ones where you need them.

owner_promoted_by_system.subject: You are now an owner of {{.workspace}}
owner_promoted_by_system.intro: The workspace {{.workspace}} had no active owner left, so you were made one as its longest-standing member. Owners can manage other owners and delete the workspace.

invitation.subject: {{.inviter}} invited you to join {{.workspace}} on dimmi
invitation.intro: {{.inviter}} invited you to join the workspace {{.workspace}} on dimmi as {{.role}}.
invitation.unexpected: If you did not expect this invitation, you can ignore this email.

invitation_accepted.subject: {{.member}} joined {{.workspace}}
invitation_accepted.intro: {{.member}} accepted your invitation and joined the workspace {{.workspace}}.
